note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  
  • Loss of appetite (~3.5 months) and unintentional weight loss (~1 stone/6 kg over ~6 months)  
  • Fatigue/low energy, low mood, occasional headaches and nausea  
  • Episodic palpitations with perceived breathlessness in elevators; no exertional dyspnoea, no chest pain  
  • History of primary hypothyroidism; stopped levothyroxine several months ago  
  • Sedentary lifestyle since symptom onset  
- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  
  • Levothyroxine (previous; dose/route/frequency not documented) – patient stopped taking several months ago  
  • No other medications or OTC agents reported  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Married; reports reduced libido (“wife complaining about nightly activities”). No STI or contraception history recorded  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Currently not walking/exercising; poor appetite and reduced intake noted  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Not recorded  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Feeling “down,” low energy, hesitant to label as depression; no self-harm ideation reported  
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Married; 35-year-old lawyer; recent job change (~3.5 months) with possible work-related stress  

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded (patient reports ~6 kg weight loss)  
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded  
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded  
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded  
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded (routine panel planned)  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not applicable (male)  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded  
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not applicable  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Clinician requested “general set of bloods” including CBC, U&E, LFTs, thyroid profile, vitamin levels; not yet performed  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 35-year-old man with fatigue, low mood, anorexia, weight loss, episodic palpitations, and prior hypothyroidism off treatment. No red-flag GI or cardiopulmonary symptoms elicited.  

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
• Major depressive disorder – High likelihood given persistent low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight changes, and situational stressors.  
• Relapsed/undertreated hypothyroidism (levothyroxine cessation) – Moderate likelihood; explains fatigue/low mood but less typical for weight loss and palpitations.  
• Iron-deficiency or other anaemia – Moderate likelihood; could contribute to fatigue and palpitations.  
• Panic attacks/anxiety disorder – Possible contributor to lift-related palpitations and breathlessness.  

Working impression: Low mood/depressive symptoms with possible contributing untreated hypothyroidism; other medical causes (anaemia, metabolic) to be excluded with blood tests.  

Management Plan

• Order comprehensive blood panel (CBC, U&E, LFTs, TSH/free T4, ferritin, B12, folate, vitamin D, glucose/lipids as indicated).  
• Reinforce need to arrange phlebotomy via support line; results to trigger follow-up appointment.  
• Advise patient to seek urgent care (A&E) if new chest pain, worsening palpitations, syncope, or significant GI changes develop.  
• Discuss potential re-initiation of levothyroxine pending thyroid function results.  
• Screen formally for depression and anxiety at follow-up; consider mental health referral based on results.  
• Encourage gradual return to physical activity as tolerated and balanced diet once appetite improves.  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): To be considered after formal screening  
- CTG registration: Not recorded  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Major depressive disorder – High likelihood: Low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, fatigue, situational stressors.  
2. Relapsed/undertreated hypothyroidism – Moderate likelihood: History of hypothyroidism and medication cessation; symptoms overlap with depression.  
3. Iron-deficiency/other anaemia – Moderate likelihood: Chronic fatigue, possible palpitations and headaches; to be assessed with CBC and iron studies.  

Quality checks

● Missing expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse), BMI/waist circumference, immunisation review, alcohol and smoking history, detailed mental-health screening, eye/ear/oral exams, urinalysis.  
● No direct contradictions noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Audio clear overall; occasional interruptions and overlapping speech but clinical content understandable.
